notes.ndidde: Recent past: today or just now.

guidebook.intro: Talk about what you did. Runyankore has a recent past for today and a far past for yesterday and before.

tips.title: Today’s past: -ire
body: For things that happened today or just now, the verb ends in **-ire** (or **-ize, -ire, -ere** depending on the stem): **Ndiire** (I’ve eaten), **Nyweire** (I’ve drunk), **Nkozire** (I’ve worked), **Nsomire** (I’ve read).
**Oriire?** asks “have you eaten?”, a common way to show care.

tips.title: Yesterday and before: -ka-
body: For yesterday or earlier, add **-ka-**: **Nkagyenda** (I went), **Nkarya** (I ate), **Nkasoma** (I read). Other persons: **okagyenda** (you went), **akagyenda** (he went), **tukagyenda** (we went).

culture.title: Oriire?
body: Asking **Oriire?** (have you eaten?) is a sign of care, and an invitation may follow. If you have, say **Ego, ndiire, webale**.
